trigger: Impermissible acquisition, access, use, or disclosure of PHI, including client PHI held as a business associate
deadline: Before deciding not to notify; document as soon as the scope is known
notify: Internal decision log (no external recipient)

trigger: Breach of the company's own unsecured PHI (company patients). For client patients the client is the covered entity and gives this notice unless the client BAA delegates it to the company
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected individual (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10 or more have out-of-date contact information)
clock_starts: Discovery: first day the breach is known, or by reasonable diligence would have been known, to any workforce member or agent (164.404(a)(2))
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more (CAD holds about 450,000 patients from 3 years of incidents)

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: Breach affecting fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS Secretary through the OCR breach portal
clock_starts: End of the calendar year of discovery

trigger: Breach involving more than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets serving that state or jurisdiction
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 500 Florida residents
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with the Chief Operating Officer

trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede a criminal investigation or damage national security
deadline: Delay for the period in a written statement; if the statement is oral, document it and delay no longer than 30 days unless a written statement follows
notify: Hold notices; record the request in the decision log
clock_starts: Date of the law enforcement statement

obligation: Business associate breach notice to billing services clients (outbound)

deadline: HIPAA: without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, with the identity of each affected individual. Client BAAs: within 10 business days of discovery (the shorter clock controls)
notify: Each affected client's privacy officer, in writing
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - business associate of 4 municipal clients
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with the Director of Revenue Cycle

obligation: Security incident report to billing services clients (outbound)
trigger: Security incident involving a client's ePHI, even if not a breach
deadline: Client BAAs: within 10 business days of discovery; summary reports of unsuccessful attempts quarterly
notify: Each affected client's privacy officer

obligation: Business associate breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor business associate (billing platform, ePCR, CAD vendor, MSSP, phone vendor) discovers a breach of company or client PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery by the vendor (BAAs may set shorter terms; target 5 business days for Tier 1 vendors)
notify: The company (Compliance and Privacy Officer)
clock_starts: Vendor discovery; the company's own clock starts when it knows or should have known

trigger: Any decision to notify or not to notify
deadline: Keep the decision log and copies of notices for 6 years
notify: Internal records

trigger: Breach of security of personal information (includes medical information and health insurance information) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred; 15 more days are available only if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days (501.171(3)(a)). Notice under the rules of the primary or functional federal regulator (HIPAA) is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - confirm the deemed-compliance path with counsel
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida

notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
owner: Compliance and Privacy Officer with counsel

trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies

notify: Each affected client

notify: The company

notify: Residents and regulators per each state's law
